newsitem.title: sri lanka: Arafat says ready to meet Netanyahu over peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says ready to meet Netanyahu over peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday he was ready to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss peace in the Middle East.

"Why not. If this is for peace I am ready, but if it is for propaganda, it is something different," Arafat said at a news conference in the Sri Lankan capital Colombo before leaving for Bangladesh after a 24-hour visit to the island.
But Arafat also accused Israel of fomenting confrontation between Palestinian groups, saying Tel Aviv wanted civil war.

"The Israeli government is looking to having instability and confrontation between the Palestinians, a civil war, which we cannot accept," Arafat said when asked about Israel's demand that he clamp down on militant groups such as the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement.
A member of Hamas carried out a suicide attack in Tel Aviv last week that killed three women.
"Peace is an open target. Our target is a comprehensive, lasting peace in the area," Arafat said.
"We have worked hard for peace and don't forget that majority of the Israeli people are for peace."
Israel has said it had not closed its door on restoring severed contacts with the Palestinian Authority despite a deepening rift after the Tel Aviv suicide attack.
Arafat said the Palestinian Authority had taken action against those who were opposed to the law, including Hamas.

Israel has accused Arafat of giving a "green signal" to militants to launch attacks on the Jewish state. Arafat also said he was not overly worried over the U.S. decision to veto Israel's condemnation by the United Nations over Tel Aviv's plans to build a settlement in Arab east Jerusalem.
"The U.S. used the veto twice in one week. But we cannot forget that President Clinton is pushing to achieve peace in our area," he said.
U.S. officials have said they expect Arafat to re-arrest guerrilla operatives he freed who are responsible for terror bombings against Israel.
